## JNJ — Quantitative Fundamental-Attractiveness Report

**Decision date: 2026-06-12 | Latest filing: 2026-03-29 (Q4) | Latest price: 2026-06-11**

---

### 1. Revenue, Earnings, Margins, Cash Flow, and Balance-Sheet Trajectory

**Revenue** is essentially flat on a sequential basis. Q4 revenue was $24.06B versus Q3's $23.99B (+0.3% QoQ). The four-quarter trajectory shows a step-up from Q1 ($21.89B) to Q2 ($23.74B, +8.5%), after which the top line has plateaued. TTM revenue totals $93.69B.

**Earnings** require careful interpretation. Q1 (period_end 2025-03-30) reported EPS of $4.54, net income of $11.00B, and operating income of $13.63B — values roughly double the subsequent three quarters. This is almost certainly a one-time item (likely a gain on a divestiture or restructuring event). Stripping Q1, the "normalized" three-quarter run-rate is EPS of $2.14/$2.12/$2.29, annualizing to roughly $8.73/share. Q4 EPS of $2.14 improved only +0.9% QoQ from Q3's $2.12.

**Margins are compressing.** Q4 gross profit fell -4.4% QoQ despite a +0.3% revenue increase, implying cost-of-revenue rose from $7.30B to $8.11B (+11.1% QoQ). Gross margin declined to 66.3% from 69.5% in Q3. Operating margin narrowed to 24.9% (Q4) from 31.2% (Q3). The ratio panel confirms the slide: net_margin fell from 0.273 (persisting from Oct-25 through Apr-26) to 0.218 as of the latest observation, and ROE dropped from 0.317 to 0.259.

**Cash flow generation deteriorated sharply.** Q4 operating cash flow was $2.51B versus Q3's $9.17B, a -72.6% QoQ decline. TTM operating cash flow remains $19.73B, but the most recent quarter's weakness warrants attention. Free cash flow data is unavailable.

**Balance sheet remains solid.** Total equity of $81.19B (up from $78.11B a year ago) and cash of $22.05B provide a cushion. Total liabilities of $119.71B give a debt-to-equity ratio of roughly 1.47x. The cash balance dropped from $38.78B in Q1 (likely bolstered by the one-time event) to a steadier $18.6B-$22B range in Q2-Q4.

### 2. Earnings Quality and Balance-Sheet Resilience

The Q1 distortion materially inflates the TTM picture. TTM net income of $26.92B includes approximately $11.00B from Q1 — more than double the normalized quarterly run-rate of ~$5.3B. Investors relying on trailing multiples computed from TTM figures are likely overstating sustainable earnings power. Adjusting for this, recurring EPS power is closer to $8.70-$9.20/share rather than the ~$11 implied by TTM.

ROE has fallen from 0.317 to 0.259 alongside margin compression, and the current ROE range of 0.3-0.3 over the window (ratio panel) suggests this decline is at the lower end of its recent corridor. The balance sheet is resilient — ample cash, investment-grade cost of capital (DBAA at 6.0% provides context), and growing equity — but the deterioration in cash conversion in Q4 ($2.51B operating cash flow on $5.24B net income = only 48% conversion) is a yellow flag.

### 3. Valuation Versus Own History

This is the central concern. PE diluted stands at **27.7x** — the **absolute ceiling** of its 365-day range (16.6–27.7). A year ago (2025-06-12) it was 17.4x. That is a ~59% multiple expansion in twelve months. P/B is 7.18, near its high of 7.6 (vs. 4.86 a year ago). P/S is 6.05.

Earnings yield at 3.6% now sits **below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.45%** — a negative spread of approximately 85 basis points. The risk-free rate effectively dominates JNJ's earnings yield, a condition that historically compresses such multiples.

The ratio history shows the PE expansion accelerated from ~18.8x in September 2025 to 27.7x today, roughly doubling the pace of any fundamental improvement. On normalized earnings (excluding the Q1 one-time gain), the "true" PE is closer to 27.3x — essentially the same, because the stock price has already moved to reflect what the market apparently recognizes as an inflated denominator.

### 4. Price Level and Return Context

JNJ closed at $238.33 on 2026-06-11, near its 365-day high of $251.71 and well above its low of $149.04. The quarterly price path shows a -1.5% decline from 2026-03-12 ($242.04), but prior quarters surged: +21.0% from 2025-12-09 and +13.7% from 2025-09-10. The stock has more than doubled off its trough while normalized earnings have barely moved. Price has outrun fundamentals.

### 5. Macro and Sentiment Overlays

The rate environment is hostile to stretched multiples: 10Y yield at 4.45% and 2Y at 4.05% (T10Y2Y spread = 0.40%) indicate a still-inverted but modestly positive curve. The 3.6% earnings yield versus 4.45% risk-free rate is a meaningful headwind for a defensive name that traditionally traded at a slight premium to bonds. VIX at 19.44 is moderate. Oil at ~$91.58 may be a modest input-cost headwind for J&J's consumer and supply chain.

News sentiment is broadly positive (mean score 0.566 across 86 articles), but per source weighting this is the weakest input and does not compensate for valuation or margin concerns.

### 6. Strongest Quantitative Upside and Downside

**Upside:** The balance sheet is genuinely strong (cash=$22.05B, equity growing), and the franchise delivers a TTM operating cash flow of $19.73B against a ~$585B market cap. If margins stabilize and the Q4 cash-flow shortfall proves seasonal or transitory, the defensive earnings stream supports a premium — just not this premium.

**Downside:** (a) PE at 27.7x is at the top of its range with no margin of safety; a reversion to the 12-month median (~20x) implies ~28% downside on the stock absent earnings growth. (b) The Q1 one-time gain flatters TTM metrics; as it rolls off, reported earnings will mechanically decline, potentially triggering multiple compression. (c) Operating cash flow collapsed -72.6% QoQ, and if Q4's cost pressure persists, further margin erosion is likely. (d) Earnings yield below the risk-free rate removes the traditional valuation floor for defensive compounders.

### 7. Provisional Conclusion

JNJ's fundamental attractiveness is **poor at current levels**. The business itself is stable — revenue is range-bound but durable, margins are high, and the balance sheet is strong. However, the stock has undergone nearly 60% multiple expansion over the past year (PE 17.4x → 27.7x) with flat-to-declining underlying profitability. Margins are compressing, operating cash flow just cratered QoQ, and TTM earnings are artificially inflated by a one-time item. At an earnings yield of 3.6% — 85bp below the 10-year Treasury — the market is paying more for JNJ's earnings stream than for risk-free cash flows, a condition unsupported by the fundamental trajectory. The quantitative case points to overvaluation versus the company's own history with deteriorating earnings quality, not the kind of mispricing that merits fundamental interest.

# Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) — Qualitative Franchise & Risk Assessment

**Decision Date: 2026-06-12 | Analyst: Qualitative**

---

## 1. Business / Franchise Read

Johnson & Johnson is a post-consumer-health-spinoff healthcare powerhouse operating through two segments: **Innovative Medicine** (~64% of 2025 sales) and **MedTech** (~36%). The 2023 Kenvue separation was a defining structural move, refocusing the company on higher-margin, innovation-driven pharmaceuticals and medical devices. The franchise is wide and deep.

**Scale & diversification.** Full-year 2025 reported sales reached $94.19 billion; Q1 2026 came in at $24.06 billion, up 9% year-over-year, with the company lifting its 2026 guidance midpoint to ~$100.8 billion in reported sales. The U.S. accounted for ~57% of 2025 revenue, with Europe and Asia-Pacific providing meaningful geographic spread. Forbes lists 2026 revenue at $96.4 billion (trailing basis) with $21 billion in profits, confirming durable profitability.

**Therapeutic moats.** In Innovative Medicine, oncology ($25.38 billion in 2025 sales) and immunology are the twin engines. DARZALEX alone generated $14.35 billion in 2025. The company has articulated a goal of becoming the #1 oncology company by 2030, supported by CARVYKTI, ERLEADA, RYBREVANT/LAZCLUZE, TALVEY, and TECVAYLI. In immunology, Stelara is declining due to loss of exclusivity (LOE), but TREMFYA and newer launches (ICOTYDE in plaque psoriasis) are being positioned as successors. The structural narrative is one of managed patent cliff transition — excluding Stelara, the company reported 5% operational growth in 2025.

**MedTech breadth.** The MedTech segment ($33.79 billion in 2025) spans orthopedics (DePuy Synthes), surgery, interventional solutions (including electrophysiology via Biosense Webster), cardiovascular (post-Abiomed and Shockwave Medical integrations), and vision (ACUVUE). The Ottava robotic surgical system is a forward-looking catalyst for competing with Intuitive Surgical. Electrophysiology products reportedly saw 16%+ growth in recent periods.

**Competitive position.** Structural sources describe JNJ as holding #1 or #2 market-share positions across most categories in which it competes. The company is unique in the industry for carrying a AAA-rated balance sheet, enabling aggressive bolt-on M&A regardless of economic cycles. Net profitability (21.83% profit margin) exceeds AbbVie (5.79%) and compares favorably to diversified peers.

**Capital allocation philosophy.** Management emphasizes disciplined allocation — R&D investment, targeted acquisitions (Shockwave, Abiomed), and 64 consecutive years of dividend increases (most recently a 3.1% hike in April 2026, payable June 9). The company is gradually monetizing its remaining Kenvue minority stake, with proceeds directed toward share repurchases and pipeline investment. This is a mature, shareholder-return-oriented capital framework anchored by robust cash generation.

---

## 2. Recent Developments (News + Updates, Dated)

**Pipeline catalysts (late May–early June 2026).** Three positive clinical readouts in rapid succession:
- **May 31:** Phase 3 PROTEUS study showed ERLEADA combined with hormone therapy before/after prostate cancer surgery reduced metastasis/death risk by 20% and increased pathologic complete response 9-fold vs. hormone therapy alone — potentially shifting a decades-long treatment paradigm (presented at ASCO, published in NEJM).
- **June 3:** Phase 2 JASMINE study showed nipocalimab significantly reduced SLE disease activity at 24 weeks, sustained through 52 weeks, with greater efficacy in autoantibody-positive patients (~80% of SLE population). Phase 3 GARDENIA is ongoing; FDA Fast Track Designation granted January 2026.
- **June 11:** Phase 2/3 ENERGY study met primary endpoint — IMAAVY (nipocalimab) achieved durable hemoglobin improvements 3× vs. placebo in warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia. FDA has granted Priority Review for supplemental BLA.

These readouts strengthen the Innovative Medicine pipeline narrative across oncology and immunology/autoimmune indications.

**Legal landscape (June 7).** A Los Angeles jury found Johnson & Johnson not negligent in a talc cancer lawsuit, contributing to a 2.02% share price gain ($232.77) on a day the S&P 500 fell 2.61%. This is one data point but directionally reduces — does not eliminate — the talc overhang narrative.

**Leadership transition (recent).** Jennifer Taubert, EVP and Worldwide Chairman of Innovative Medicine, announced retirement after 21 years; Tom Cavanaugh is her designated successor. Leadership continuity in the pharma segment will be watched.

**Defensive rotation.** JNJ has been a beneficiary of the broader market's rotation into defensive/healthcare names. The stock's 57.4% one-year total shareholder return and 15.0% YTD return reflect both fundamental re-rating and defensive demand.

---

## 3. Material Qualitative Risks & Offsets

| Risk | Detail | Offset |
|---|---|---|
| **Talc litigation** | Ongoing multi-billion-dollar legal exposure from ovarian cancer lawsuits. While recent jury verdicts have gone JNJ's way and management has explored structured settlements, the ultimate liability remains uncertain and weighs on valuation. | AAA balance sheet provides ample absorption capacity; recent not-negligible verdict (June 7) is directionally positive; settlements could bring finality. |
| **Stelara LOE** | Stelara biosimilar competition is an acknowledged headwind — sales declined to $6.08 billion in 2025 (down 3%). Alvotech/Teva biosimilar licensing is progressing. | Ex-Stelara operational growth was 5% in 2025; TREMFYA, ICOTYDE, and newer immunology assets are being scaled to absorb the gap. |
| **Upcoming LOEs (Opsumit, Simponi)** | Additional patent expirations could create further revenue erosion in coming years. | Pipeline breadth (nipocalimab, oncology portfolio) and MedTech growth diversify the risk. |
| **MedTech China softness** | Cited as a headwind in multiple structural sources; procedure volumes and pricing in China face uncertainty. | U.S. remains the dominant revenue engine (~57%); MedTech innovation pipeline (Ottava, electrophysiology, Shockwave) could offset geography-specific weakness. |
| **Regulatory / drug pricing** | U.S. drug-pricing policy debates and Medicare negotiation create persistent uncertainty for pharma margins. | Company's dual pharma/medtech structure and global diversification provide partial insulation; defensive healthcare demand is structurally resilient. |
| **Concentration risk** | DARZALEX at $14.35 billion represents a meaningful share of Innovative Medicine revenue. Any safety signal or competitive disruption would be material. | Broad oncology and immunology pipelines (ERLEADA, CARVYKTI, nipocalimab franchise) are being built to reduce single-product dependency over time. |

---

## 4. Qualitative Assessment

**Overall: Positive — durable franchise with manageable transition risks.**

The narrative supports fundamental attractiveness. JNJ is a structurally sound, diversified healthcare franchise with unmatched scale, a AAA balance sheet, and a post-spinoff strategic clarity that concentrates capital on higher-margin innovation. The pipeline is delivering — three positive Phase 2/3 readouts in oncology and autoimmune disease within a two-week window reinforce the thesis that the company can grow through the Stelara LOE and future patent cliffs. Q1 2026 results ($24.1B revenue, 9% growth, guidance lift) confirm operational momentum is not merely aspirational.

The talc litigation remains the most material qualitative overhang, but the balance sheet's capacity to absorb it, combined with recent favorable jury outcomes, suggests this is a priced-in risk rather than an existential one. The MedTech robotics and cardiovascular integration story (Ottava, Abiomed, Shockwave) adds a structural growth vector that differentiates JNJ from pure-play pharma peers.

**The franchise quality is high; the risk/reward skews positive for a long-duration fundamental holder.**

---

However, the stock is extremely unattractive at current levels on all three pillars. Pillar 1 (fundamentals): revenue is flat QoQ ($24.06B Q4 vs $23.99B Q3), margins are compressing (gross margin 66.3% vs 69.5% QoQ, operating margin 24.9% vs 31.2%), operating cash flow collapsed -72.6% QoQ ($2.51B vs $9.17B), and TTM earnings are artificially inflated by a Q1 one-time item ($11B net income vs normalized ~$5.3B quarterly run-rate). ROE has declined from 0.317 to 0.259. Pillar 2 (valuation): PE diluted stands at 27.7x — the absolute ceiling of its 365-day range (16.6–27.7) and ~59% above the 17.4x level of a year ago — with no corresponding fundamental improvement to justify it. Earnings yield of 3.6% sits 85bp below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.45%, removing the traditional defensive valuation floor. On normalized earnings the true PE is essentially the same ~27x. P/B at 7.18 is near its high. Pillar 3 (near-term catalyst): The Q1 one-time gain rolls off TTM in coming quarters, mechanically depressing reported earnings and likely triggering multiple compression — this is a near-term downside catalyst, not an upside one. The combination of deteriorating earnings quality, margin compression, cash flow weakness, and extreme valuation versus own history with a pending negative earnings event makes JNJ strongly unattractive.
